correctness.rationale: Every nonextreme cycle-to-cycle coloring is uniquely an initial color and a fixed-size negative-edge subset. Actual one-cell changes swap adjacent unequal increments, so each is exactly one exclusion-particle step and changes the initial color by two only at the index cut. The rotation quotient is the standard cubical unordered particle model; Abrams–Prue–Scrimshaw applies for m≥r+1, giving fundamental group Z with primitive winding D=Δ/m. Cover monodromy by +2 modulo n forces D to be divisible by n/gcd(n,2) in a lifted closed loop. Thus edge length is at least |q|mn/gcd(n,2), attained by an explicitly described m-step positive particle circuit repeated n/gcd(n,2) times and |q| times. All boundaries 1≤r<m,n≥5 are addressed. Finite direct-recoloring and signed BFS checks passed for odd/even targets but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For graph-coloring reconfiguration, minimizing the length of a nontrivial return path is a natural geometric complexity question not determined by the homotopy class alone. The result gives an exact, sector-independent answer and complete generator-power length spectrum for infinitely many cycle pairs, revealing a uniform odd/even halving and an explicit optimal sequence. The exclusion-particle covering argument is structural and reusable for reconfiguration metrics; no unsupported downstream theorem is needed.
